title: USB VIP example tb_usb_svt_uvm_basic_router_sys -- hub/multi-tier env, 3 distinct scoreboard architectures, hand-coded hub enumeration sequence
summary:
tb_usb_svt_uvm_basic_router_sys is the deepest environment example: hub/multi-tier USB topology with parameterized agent ARRAYS (not singletons) -- svt_usb_hub_agent hub_agent[`SVT_USB_NUM_HUB_INST], svt_usb_agent dev_agent[`SVT_USB_NUM_DEVICE_INST], plus optional passive dev_mon_agent[i]/host_mon_agent gated by cfg.enable_{host,dev}_mon flags. Per-instance uvm_config_db paths use $psprintf-built index strings, e.g. `string_dev_cfg=$psprintf('dev_agent[%0d]',i); uvm_config_db#(...)::set(this,string_dev_cfg,'cfg',cfg.dev_cfg[i]);` -- the general idiom for configuring N-way agent arrays.

REMOTE_CFG CLONING CHAIN (env/usb_hub_basic_env.sv build_phase): for every link boundary using PIPE3/PIPE4/UTMI, the env clones the peer config ($cast(remote_cfg, cfg.hub_cfg[i].upstream_cfg.clone())), forces remote_cfg.component_subtype=PHY, validates it (remote_cfg.is_valid(0)), then registers it under the OTHER side's agent path ('downstream_remote_cfg[j]', 'upstream_remote_cfg', 'remote_cfg' depending on link) -- repeated ~6 times for host-to-hub-upstream, hub-downstream-to-next-hub-upstream, and last-hub-downstream-to-device links. This is the general mechanism for wiring MAC/PHY split VIP topologies at ANY tier depth.

CALLBACK: end_of_elaboration_phase (not build_phase) attaches a THIRD distinct callback base class -- svt_usb_link_callbacks (vs protocol_callbacks and physical_callbacks seen elsewhere): `pkts_cb=new(); uvm_callbacks#(svt_usb_link)::add(hub_agent[0].downstream_agent[0].link, pkts_cb);` where pkt_callback extends svt_usb_link_callbacks overrides pre_usb_ss_tx_packet_transform(component, packet, ref bit drop) to set packet.inter_pkt_delay=100ns.

3 DISTINCT SCOREBOARD ARCHITECTURES (all in env/): usb_transaction_scoreboard.sv and usb_transfer_scoreboard.sv use uvm_analysis_imp_decl-based dual queues (host/dev) + events, a forever-loop pop-and-linear-search match on (device_address, endpoint_number, xact_type), uvm_comparer with .physical=1/.abstract=0 ('RELEVANT' policy), address filtering against a device_cfg[] array via set_device_cfg(). usb_packet_scoreboard.sv splits 8 ways (SS/20-tx/rx x host/dev), runs 4 concurrent fork/join match blocks keyed on ept_num for TRANSACTION/DATA packets (FIFO order for other packet types like handshakes), uses a CUSTOM extend_uvm_comparer extends svt_comparer returning SVT_DATA_TYPE::RELEVANT from get_kind() -- a THIRD distinct compare-policy mechanism vs the other two scoreboards. LINK_MANAGEMENT_PACKETs explicitly excluded from comparison. Exposes flush_scoreboard() for external use 'in case of Vbus getting off in between of simulation'. Env feeds scoreboards NOT via direct VIP analysis-port connect but by re-polling uvm_event pools (NOTIFY_USB_TRANSFER_ENDED etc) inside a run_phase fork (supply_analysis_ports() task) and republishing onto its OWN analysis ports -- materially different from intermediate_sys's direct-connect pattern (see that record), used here because packet/transaction-level (not just transfer-level) multi-device comparison is needed.

CONFIGURATION: usb_hub_shared_cfg.sv adds a THIRD config array beyond host_cfg/dev_cfg[] -- svt_usb_hub_agent_configuration hub_cfg[], each with upstream_cfg (hub's own device-side config) and downstream_cfg[] (array of HOST-role configs, one per downstream port). setup_usb_ssp_defaults() configures ESSG2 (Enhanced SuperSpeed Gen2 / USB 3.2) via usb_ess_speed_max/min fields distinct from plain speed. Hub upstream ports get exactly 2 endpoints (CONTROL ep0, INTERRUPT-IN ep1 status pipe, with `ifdef SVT_USB_HUB_POLLING_ENABLE gating disable_ss_host_polling=1 -- polling-vs-ERDY hub status notification is a compile-time choice). Carries bit concurrent_test and per-scoreboard-type enable flags.

SEQUENCE: usb_directed_transfers_sequence_multi_tier_hub.sv performs FULL manual USB hub enumeration via raw svt_usb_transfer randomize-with-inline-constraints on SETUP fields: hub_set_depth() sends HUB_CLASS_SET_HUB_DEPTH (w_value==hub_depth, required per USB3 spec); hub_set_addr_set_config() does SET_ADDRESS then SET_CONFIGURATION back to back (comment notes Device VIP does not actually change its device_address from this -- that's set separately via config); enumerate_downstream_device() does SetPortFeature PORT_POWER (w_value==8) then PORT_RESET (w_value==4) for 2.0 speeds, waiting on shared_status.link_usb_20_state==DEVICE_ATTACHED/ENABLED or shared_status.ltssm_state==U0 on BOTH the hub downstream port and device/next-hub concurrently (fork...join); polling_port() implements a full interrupt-endpoint hub status-change poll loop decoding wPortChange/wPortStatus 16-bit fields from a 4-byte GET_STATUS response and issuing the matching CLEAR_FEATURE (16=connect, 19=reset-complete, 18=resume-complete). Top-level body() scales this across up to 5 hub tiers via literal `if (N>k)` cascades, not a generic loop -- a hard cap worth noting. Uses `xfer.reasonable_control_transfer.constraint_mode(0)` before inline randomize() to disable a built-in VIP constraint that would otherwise block directed hub-class w_value/w_index requests.
